root_idea.summary: The root centers on close relation or common origin between separate things.
root_idea.development: Its central image is multiple trees or shoots emerging from one root; this extends to kinship and physical proximity, while a divergent lexical branch denotes a ground depression or water-hole.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested plural is presented under the supported singular dictionary citation form صِنْوٌ.

senses.definition: One of multiple tree-shoots or trees issuing from a single root; in the Quran, a palm tree growing together with others from one root.
senses.usage_conditions: The singular names each member in relation to its companions; the Quranic plural صِنْوَانٌ is contrasted with trees having separate roots.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of palm trees: to grow in pairs, triplets, or more, emerging together from single roots.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV derived verb used of palms growing jointly from one root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A relative regarded as branching from the same stock: a brother, and by extension a son or a paternal uncle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended use referring to common lineage; the cited attestations vary in the precise specification of the brother relationship.
Attested as a meaning of the plural form أَصْنَاءٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Two wells close together, or two wells drawing water from one spring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression describing wells connected by proximity or a shared source of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A widened pit or well from which water is not drawn and whose water is unused.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Classical Arabic use, with the plural صِنْوَانٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small, unused water-hole; alternatively, a cleft, ravine, or gap between mountains in which water flows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited lexical tradition reports the water-hole and mountain-ravine interpretations as alternative applications of the diminutive.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Derived Form IV verb describing palms growing together from single roots.
Tree relationship and Quran-attested plural usage.
Extended kinship meanings based on common stock.
Plural meaning of likes or fellows.
Construction for nearby or spring-connected wells.
Specialized meaning of a widened unused well.
Diminutive denoting a small water-hole or, in an alternative interpretation, a mountain cleft or ravine.

cautions: Lane records dialectal vocalic variants of صِنْوٌ and variant plural forms; the public Quranic headword uses the supported singular citation form.
The صُنَيٌّ entry preserves alternative reported interpretations rather than resolving them into a single physical referent.
